1.title: Network Access and Management Methods
1.text: Welcome to Module sixteen: Network Access and Management Methods. It covers the exam area three point zero Network Operations. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do six things. three point five Compare and contrast network access and management methods: site-to-site V P N (virtual private network). Client-to-site V P N (clientless, split tunnel versus full tunnel). Connection methods (S S H, gooey, A P I, console). Jump box or host. In-band versus out-of-band management. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: three point zero Network Operations (nineteen percent). Exam format: up to ninety questions in ninety minutes; a score of seven hundred twenty on a scale of one hundred to nine hundred passes. Validated against: the official Comp T I A Network plus N ten to nine exam objectives, version four point zero.

1.title: VPNs
1.text: V P Ns. A virtual private network (V P N) creates an encrypted tunnel across an untrusted network.

1.title: VPNs, continued
1.text: V P Ns. The figure shows this: A site-to-site V P N between offices and a client-to-site V P N for a remote user.

1.title: VPNs, continued
1.text: V P Ns. Site-to-site V P N. Two networks (offices) connected permanently by V P N gateways; users need no client software. Client-to-site (remote access) V P N. One user connects to the office network with a V P N client. Clientless V P N. Access through a web browser (usually T L S), no software installed, often to specific applications. Full tunnel. All the client's traffic goes through the V P N; full inspection and policy, more bandwidth use. Split tunnel. Only traffic for company networks goes through the V P N; the rest goes straight to the internet; less load, less control. Exam tip: Branch offices permanently connected equals site-to-site. A traveling employee equals client-to-site. Everything must be inspected equals full tunnel.

1.title: Management connection methods
1.text: Management connection methods. S S H. Encrypted command line (port twenty-two); replaces Telnet. gooey. A graphical management interface, usually a web page over H T T P S. A P I. Programmatic management (R E S T), used by automation. Console. Direct serial or U S B connection to the device; works even with no network; used for initial setup and recovery.

1.title: Jump boxes and management paths
1.text: Jump boxes and management paths. Jump box or jump host. A hardened intermediate server admins connect to first, then reach protected devices; one controlled, logged entry point. In-band management. Management traffic travels over the production network (S S H, S N M P); fails if the network fails. Out-of-band management. A separate path (console server, dedicated management network, cellular modem); works during outages. Exam tip: "Reach a router when the production network is down" equals out-of-band (console or a separate management network). A jump box reduces the attack surface. Exam tip: Console works with no network; S S H works over the network; a jump box is the controlled entry point.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Two offices must be connected all the time without any software on user P C s. What fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: A site-to-site V P N. Site-to-site V P Ns link networks through gateways.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A traveling employee needs access to internal web applications through a browser with nothing to install. What fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: A clientless V P N. Clientless V P Ns use the browser.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Security wants all remote-user traffic inspected by the corporate firewall. Which V P N design fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: A full tunnel. Full tunnel sends all traffic through the V P N.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. An engineer must configure a router that has lost all network connectivity. What should the engineer use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: The console port. The console works without a network.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Administrators must reach servers only through one hardened, logged entry point. What fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: A jump box. A jump box provides a controlled access path.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which management approach uses a separate network that keeps working during an outage? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Out-of-band management. Out-of-band uses a separate path.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What is a split tunnel? Answer: Only company traffic uses the V P N; other traffic goes directly to the internet. Question two. What does a site-to-site V P N connect? Answer: Two networks, through V P N gateways. Question three. Which port does S S H use? Answer: twenty-two.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What is a console connection? Answer: A direct serial or U S B connection that works without a network. Question five. What is a jump host? Answer: A hardened intermediate server used to reach protected devices. Question six. What is in-band management? Answer: Management over the production network.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. V P N: site-to-site (offices), client-to-site (users), clientless (browser); full versus split tunnel. Methods: S S H (twenty-two), gooey (H T T P S), A P I, console (no network needed). Paths: jump box (controlled entry), in-band versus out-of-band.
